full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 2-9-2013 passed by the learned District Judge, Jhalakathi in Title Appeal No.27 of 2013 affirming the order No.5 dated 14-5-2013 passed by the learned Assistant Judge (in charge), Kathalia, Jhalakathi in Title Suit No.26 of 2013 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The brief fact relevant for disposal of this Rule is that the petitioner as plaintiff filed a suit being Title Suit No.26 of 2013 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kathalia impleading the opposite parties as defendants praying a decree declaring the plaintiff as daptari-cum-guard in Chonautha Government Primary School. The plaintiff's case in short is that according to the decision of the Government, the Chairman of the Managing Committee of No.27 Chonautha Government Primary School invited applications for appointment of daptari-cum-guard of No.27 Chonautha Government Primary School through a written notice dated 2-12-2012 and having learn about the notice dated 2-12-2012 the plaintiff-petitioner, opposite party No.6 and one Md Alamgir Hossain applied for the post of daptari-cum-guard in No.27 Chonautha Government Primary School; that as per circular dated 09-12-2012 for the purpose of appointment of daptari-cum-guard in the Government Primary School throughout the country; the recruitment examination committee Headmaster and Member Secretary of No.27 Chonautha Government Primary School issued a notice on 20-12-2012 directing the applicants to appear before the recruitment examination committee on 26-12-2012 at 10-00 am at the office of Upazila Education Officer, Kathalia to take part in the viva-voce examination and thereafter, the petitioner and opposite party No.6 duly appeared before the recruitment examination committee on 26-12-2012 and took part in the viva-voce examination while another candidate namely, Md Alamgir Hossain did not appear before the recruitment examination committee and the present petitioner obtained 16(sixteen) marks out of 20(twenty) marks stood 1st position and opposite party No.6 obtained 11 (eleven) marks out of 20(twenty) marks and he stood 2nd position and the recruitment examination committee informed the result of viva-voce examination to the present petitioner and supplied a copy of resolution (Annexure-D), result sheet (Annexure-D1) and merit list (Annexure-D2) to the plaintiff-petitioner and also informed to the plaintiff-petitioner that he will be appointed as daptari-cum-guard of No.27 Chonautha Government Primary School in due course of time as he stood 1st position in the viva-voce examination. In this background some days after the plaintiff-petitioner went to the Chairman of the Managing Committee of No.27 Chonautha Government Primary School to know about his appointment in the post of daptari-cum-guard while the Chairman (opposite party No.5) expressed with regret that it will not be possible on his part to appoint the plaintiff in the post of daptari-cum-guard of No.27 Chonautha Government Primary School due to his high hands and undue influence of the leaders of the ruling party. Thereafter, the plaintiff- petitioner came to know from reliable source that though the plaintiff stood 1st in the recruitment examination yet opposite party No.6 will be appointed as daptari-cum-guard of No.27 Chonautha Government Primary School in place of the plaintiff and hence, the suit. 

 7. The learned Assistant Judge after hearing as to maintainability of the suit by order No.5 dated 14-5-2013 dismissed the suit on the finding that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner. The plaintiff thereupon, took an appeal being Title Appeal No.27 of 2013 therefrom. The learned District Judge, Jhalakathi by the impugned judgment and decree dated 2-9-2013 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the order of the trial Court on the findings that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner inasmuch as after examination a candidate cannot sought for a decree to appoint him in job. 

 8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree dated 2-9-2013 the plaintiff-petitioner has come before this Court and obtained the present rule. 

 15. It appears that in this case the defendants neither filed any written statement nor filed any application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Defendant No.6 (opposite party No.6) entered appearance in the suit on 5-5-2013 and filed time petition for submitting written statement and the learned Assistant Judge after hearing allowed the application and fixed on 14-5-2013 for hearing as to the maintainability of the suit. In this backdrop the learned Assistant Judge at his own motion after hearing as to maintainability of the suit by order No.5 dated 14-5-2013 dismissed the suit on the finding that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner. The plaintiff thereupon, took an appeal being Title Appeal No.27 of 2013 therefrom and the learned District Judge, Jhalakathi by the impugned judgment and decree dated 2-9-2013 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the order of the trial Court on the observation that; 

 20. In the result, the rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree of the appellate Court dated 2-9-2013 as well as the order No.5 dated 14-5-2013 passed by the learned Assistant Judge (in charge), Kathalia, Jhalakathi in Title Suit No.26 of 2013 are set-aside without any order as to cost.
